flag.backup_encrypt: encrypt the backup with a passphrase (taken from KUT_BACKUP_PASSWORD or asked)
flag.restore_endpoint: replace the endpoint in the backup with this one (the new IP or hostname when moving servers)

backup.encrypted_note: The backup is encrypted with a passphrase. If you lose the passphrase the backup cannot be opened; Kut cannot recover it.
backup.plain_warning: WARNING: The backup contains the server's private key and the preshared keys and is NOT ENCRYPTED. Keep it somewhere safe or encrypt it with -encrypt.

done.one:
Restored: {n} file → {data}
Now start the service: sudo systemctl start kut (the wg configuration is rewritten at startup)
done.other:
Restored: {n} files → {data}
Now start the service: sudo systemctl start kut (the wg configuration is rewritten at startup)

clibackup.not_data_dir: {data} is not a Kut data directory: {err}
clibackup.service_running: the kut service is running; stop it first: sudo systemctl stop kut
clibackup.not_empty: {data} is not empty; add -force to overwrite it (existing files are kept as .bak)
